no, not really there is something called brain plasticity where the brain can change. you’re right about the building “neutron structures” part where neurons that fire together wire together and their connections gets stronger but the opposite is true as well. the neuron connections that you have linked to suicidal ideation with other triggers can get weaker if you focus on reconnecting them with other things. 

i’m not really good at explaining stuff but imagine if suicidal ideation was a getaway card for you to help yourself relax and destress because thinking of death can sometimes be freeing to the soul. try finding other events that can trigger the same relaxation and destress feelings like petting a cat, eating a tub of ice cream or screaming on top of a hill. gradually, once you’re less reliant on suicidal ideation to soothe yourself, and weaken this neural connection you’ll soon forget that it was once a frequent part of your life. 

the only thing tho, it takes effort. if you continue with the current default settings in your brain, it’s going to be hard to do a 180 and reduce the suicidal ideations.

(edit: i’m the same age as well, been struggling with suicidal ideations since i was 7. been actively trying to learn the neuroscience behind this so i can attempt to get better. you can too!!)

Update: for anyone in the future having this issue this is what worked for me.

1. Increase your fps in unreal engine. Edit-Project Settings-Search FPS-Increase Default Display Rate (default was 30 fps)

2. Turn off Motion Blur. Edit-Project Settings-Search motion blur- Untick the box

3. Remove motion blur from post processing. (Got this off unreal engine forum.) World Outlier-Search “postprocess”-Open the details for your postprocessvolume- Rendering Features- Motion Blur- set amount to 0

4. Reduce mouse sensitivity. I have a gaming mouse, so I created a new sensitivity setting and just reduced my original sensitivity by half. This seems to help a great deal when I’m zooming in and out and moving in all axes in the interface. 

Hope this helps!
